from.place: The K-flat resolution construction: extending a prescribed flat replacement of a good truncation by one stage, before forming the telescope

title: One compatible extension of a bounded-above flat truncation replacement
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Assume that every R-module sheaf M admits an epimorphism P -> M with P flat. Let G be a cochain complex of R-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], n a natural number, and E a bounded-above complex with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Suppose q:E -> truncLE(n)G is a termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. There exist a bounded-above complex E' with flat terms, a map t:E -> E', and a termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism q':E' -> truncLE(n+1)G such that t followed by q' and the truncation inclusion into G equals q followed by the n-th truncation inclusion into G. The previous complex E and augmentation q are prescribed. This asserts only one extension, not an infinite tower.

source.place: Lemma 06XX (derived-lemma-special-direct-system), induction step; specialization to flat module sheaves as in Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 077J

proof.text: Compose the prescribed augmentation q with the inclusion into the next good truncation. Its mapping cone is bounded above because E and the next truncation are bounded above. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] at any common upper bound to obtain a termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism Q -> C with bounded-above flat Q.

The map Q -> C -> E[1] defines the extension triangle E -> E' -> Q -> E[1]. Represent its first map by a degreewise split injection with cokernel Q. The resulting terms of E' are isomorphic to E^i plus Q^i, so [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat] gives flatness; their common upper bound gives boundedness. The morphism of triangles to E -> truncLE(n+1)G -> C gives an augmentation f. Extend its augmentation-square homotopy along the degreewise retractions and subtract the homotopy differential from f; this makes the square commute strictly. Long exact cohomology sequences, identity on E, and the quasi-isomorphism Q -> C show that f is a quasi-isomorphism. These are precisely the triangle construction and homotopy correction in 06XX.

Strict commutativity and termwise epimorphy of q make f epic away from degrees n and n+1. Apply the explicitly assumed flat-cover property to G^n and obtain P -> G^n with flat P and epic map. Add its identity disk in degrees n and n+1, with augmentation the cover in degree n and its differential in degree n+1. This disk covers degree n and the boundaries in degree n+1. The epimorphism H^(n+1)(f) supplies the remaining cycles, so the sum augmentation is epic in degree n+1 as well. The disk is contractible, so the new augmentation remains a quasi-isomorphism. The finite direct sums remain flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat], and boundedness is preserved. The original E includes through the old summand, so the strict square remains valid. Compose it with the inclusion into G to obtain the asserted equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_flat_truncation_successor
    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}}
    (hcover : ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R),
      ∃ (P : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) (p : P ⟶ M),
        SheafOfModules.IsFlat P ∧ Epi p)
    (G : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (E : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (q : E ⟶ G.truncLE (n : ℤ))
    (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (E.X i))
    (hquasi : QuasiIso q) (hepi : ∀ i : ℤ, Epi (q.f i)) :
    ∃ (E' : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ)
      (t : E ⟶ E') (q' : E' ⟶ G.truncLE ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)),
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (E'.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (E'.X i)) ∧ QuasiIso q' ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Epi (q'.f i)) ∧
      t ≫ q' ≫ G.ιTruncLE ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = q ≫ G.ιTruncLE (n : ℤ)
